issues.legal_issue: An administrative order cannot be invalidated in a collateral civil proceeding when its validity is not directly in issue and the authority that made it is not a party.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of a sale agreement and did not place the competent authority’s orders for review.
The competent authority was not joined as a party, and the orders were not challenged in an appropriate proceeding.
The orders were not found to be wholly without jurisdiction, and their validity was raised before the appellate bench without having been made an issue in the suit.
issues.conclusion: The appellate bench could not examine or effectively invalidate the competent authority’s orders in the suit or make strictures against the authority; those orders had to be set aside in an appropriate proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: An order that may be void in relation to one person may be valid in relation to another, and even a void order is not necessarily non est. Its validity cannot be determined collaterally in the absence of the authority that made it. The judgment treats this as a settled principle and cites no earlier case for it.

rule.if: civil_suit_for_specific_performance and agency_order_not_a_subject_of_the_suit and agency_not_joined and (agency_order_not_directly_challenged or agency_order_not_wholly_without_authority)

predicates.civil_suit_for_specific_performance: The proceeding is a civil suit seeking specific performance of an agreement.
predicates.agency_order_not_a_subject_of_the_suit: The validity of the administrative order was not made an issue for decision in the suit.
predicates.agency_not_joined: The authority that made the order was not joined as a party to the suit.
predicates.agency_order_not_directly_challenged: The order was not directly challenged in an appropriate proceeding.
predicates.agency_order_not_wholly_without_authorit: The order was not found to have been made wholly without jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit does not put an administrative order directly in issue, the order-making authority is absent, and the order is not wholly without authority, the order cannot be invalidated collaterally in that suit.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance cannot be decreed on the basis of a contract requiring regulatory permission when that permission has been expressly refused and the refusal remains effective.
material_facts: The agreement made the sale subject to permission from the competent authority and provided for repayment of the advance if permission was refused.
The authority refused permission, stating that the agreed vacant land was not available for transfer under the land-ceiling proceedings.
The refusal had not been set aside in an appropriate proceeding.
The trial court and the single judge refused specific performance, while the appellate bench granted it.
issues.conclusion: On the face of the effective refusal of permission, specific performance could not be granted; the appellate bench’s decree was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 gives courts discretionary jurisdiction over specific performance, and relevant subsequent events and competent-authority orders may be considered in exercising it. A court may make a decree subject to permission where permission has not already been expressly refused, as in Mrs. Chandnee Vidya Vati Madden v. Dr. C.L. Katial and Nirmal Anand v. Advent Corporation (P) Ltd.; those decisions do not extend to an effective express refusal. HPA International v. Bhagwandas Fatehchand Daswani was distinguished on its facts. The court also referred to New Zealand Shipping Co., Ltd. v. Scoiete Des Ateliers Et. Chantiers De France on the principle that a party should not take advantage of its own wrong, but found that principle did not overcome the express refusal in this case.

rule.if: specific_performance_claim and contract_requires_regulatory_permission and permission_expressly_refused and refusal_order_remains_effective

predicates.specific_performance_claim: The claimant seeks a decree requiring performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.contract_requires_regulatory_permission: The agreement makes the sale dependent on permission from a competent authority.
predicates.permission_expressly_refused: The competent authority expressly refused the required permission.
predicates.refusal_order_remains_effective: The refusal has not been set aside in an appropriate proceeding.

issues.definition: If a specific-performance claim concerns an agreement dependent on regulatory permission that has been expressly refused and the refusal remains effective, a decree for specific performance is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: An intra-court appellate bench should not ordinarily disturb a discretionary refusal of specific performance by the courts below without a valid basis for intervention.
material_facts: The trial court refused specific performance and granted alternative monetary relief, and the single judge dismissed the claimant’s appeal.

The appellate bench reversed that discretionary decision and granted specific performance after relying on matters it was not entitled to determine in the suit, including the validity of the authority’s orders.
The appellate bench’s reasoning did not provide a sound basis for displacing the lower courts’ exercise of discretion.
issues.conclusion: The appellate bench’s interference with the lower courts’ discretionary decision could not be sustained, and its judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 confers discretionary jurisdiction, which must not be exercised on whims or caprice but may take account of relevant circumstances and subsequent events. An appellate court exercising intra-court jurisdiction may review findings of fact and law, but should ordinarily not interfere with discretion exercised by the courts below. The judgment relies on Manjunath Anandappa Urf Shivappa Hanasi v. Tammanasa and Others for the relevance of reasonable timing and the limits on appellate interference with discretion.

predicates.intra_court_appeal: The proceeding is an intra-court appeal from a lower court’s decision.
predicates.lower_courts_exercised_discretion_agains: The courts below exercised their discretion to refuse specific performance.
predicates.appellate_interference_relies_on_irrelev: The appellate court displaced that exercise of discretion by relying on matters that were not properly within the proceeding.

issues.definition: In an intra-court appeal, when the courts below have refused specific performance as a discretionary matter and the appellate intervention relies on irrelevant matters, their discretionary ruling should not be disturbed.
